a.definition: Used before a singular countable noun when the person or thing is not already identified.
examples: I saw a bird in an old tree.

an.definition: Used before a singular countable noun when the person or thing is not already identified.
examples: I saw a bird in an old tree.

the.definition: Used before a noun to refer to a particular person or thing that the listener can identify.

i.definition: The person who is speaking or writing.

you.definition: The person or people being spoken or written to.

he.definition: A male person or animal already mentioned or understood.

she.definition: A female person or animal already mentioned or understood.

it.definition: A thing, animal, situation, time, or weather condition already mentioned or understood.

we.definition: The speaker together with one or more other people.

they.definition: People or things already mentioned; also a person whose gender is unknown or unspecified.

me.definition: The object form of I, referring to the speaker.

her.definition: The object form of she; or belonging to the female person being referred to.
examples: I asked her about her job.

us.definition: The object form of we, referring to the speaker and other people.

my.definition: Belonging to or connected with the speaker.

your.definition: Belonging to or connected with the person or people being addressed.

his.definition: Belonging to or connected with the male person being referred to.

its.definition: Belonging to or connected with the thing or animal being referred to.

our.definition: Belonging to or connected with the speaker and other people.

their.definition: Belonging to or connected with the people or person being referred to.

this.definition: The person or thing close to the speaker, or the idea just mentioned.

that.definition: Refers to a person, thing, or idea farther away or already mentioned; also introduces a clause.
examples: I know that that house is empty.

these.definition: The plural form of this, referring to people or things close to the speaker.

those.definition: The plural form of that, referring to people or things farther away or already mentioned.

and.definition: Connects words or statements that are added together.

examples: Would you like tea or coffee?

but.definition: Introduces a statement that contrasts with what was just said.

if.definition: Introduces a condition or an uncertain possibility.
examples: We will go if it stops raining.
I stayed home because I was tired.

although.definition: Introduces a fact that contrasts with the main statement.
examples: Although it was cold, we went outside.

though.definition: Introduces a fact that contrasts with the main statement.
examples: Although it was cold, we went outside.

when.definition: Asks or states at what time something happens.

while.definition: During the time that something else happens; or used to contrast two situations.

who.definition: Asks about a person, or introduces information about a person.

whom.definition: The object form of who, used especially in formal English.
examples: To whom should I send it?

whose.definition: Asks or states which person something belongs to.

what.definition: Asks about the identity, nature, or kind of something.

which.definition: Asks about or identifies one or more members of a known group.

where.definition: Asks or states in what place something is or happens.

why.definition: Asks or states the reason for something.

how.definition: Asks or states the manner, condition, degree, or amount of something.

to.definition: Shows a destination or recipient; also comes before a verb in its infinitive form.
examples: I want to go to school.

of.definition: Shows a relationship such as belonging, origin, contents, or a part of something.

in.definition: Inside a place or within a period of time.

on.definition: Touching a surface; also used for particular days or dates.
examples: The book is on the table.

at.definition: Identifies a particular place, point, activity, or time.

by.definition: Shows who does something, the method used, a nearby position, or a deadline.
examples: The book was written by her.

for.definition: Shows a purpose, recipient, reason, or length of time.

from.definition: Shows the starting point, source, or origin of something.

with.definition: Together with, having, or using something.

without.definition: Not having or not using something.

as.definition: Shows a role, manner, reason, time, or comparison.

than.definition: Introduces the second part of a comparison.
examples: This bag is heavier than mine.

not.definition: Makes a statement or part of a statement negative.

am.definition: A form of be: expresses identity, a state, or existence; also helps form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
examples: She is happy. They are studying.

is.definition: A form of be: expresses identity, a state, or existence; also helps form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
examples: She is happy. They are studying.

are.definition: A form of be: expresses identity, a state, or existence; also helps form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
examples: She is happy. They are studying.

was.definition: A form of be: expresses identity, a state, or existence; also helps form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
examples: She is happy. They are studying.

were.definition: A form of be: expresses identity, a state, or existence; also helps form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
examples: She is happy. They are studying.

been.definition: A form of be: expresses identity, a state, or existence; also helps form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
examples: She is happy. They are studying.

being.definition: A form of be: expresses identity, a state, or existence; also helps form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
examples: She is happy. They are studying.

has.definition: A form of have: means to possess or experience something; also helps form perfect tenses.
examples: She has a car. He has finished.

had.definition: A form of have: means to possess or experience something; also helps form perfect tenses.
examples: She has a car. He has finished.

does.definition: A form of do: means to perform an action; also helps form questions, negatives, and emphasis.

did.definition: A form of do: means to perform an action; also helps form questions, negatives, and emphasis.

can.definition: Expresses ability, permission, or a general possibility.

could.definition: Expresses past ability, a possibility, or a polite request.

will.definition: Expresses a future event, willingness, a promise, or a prediction.

would.definition: Expresses an imagined result, a past habit, or a polite request.
examples: I would travel if I had time.

might.definition: Expresses a possibility that is uncertain.

must.definition: Expresses a strong obligation or a conclusion based on evidence.
examples: You must wear a seat belt.

shall.definition: Expresses a future action, an offer, a suggestion, or a formal requirement.

should.definition: Expresses advice, duty, or something expected to happen.

i'm.definition: A shortened form of I am.

you're.definition: A shortened form of you are.

he's.definition: A shortened form of he is or he has.

she's.definition: A shortened form of she is or she has.

it's.definition: A shortened form of it is or it has.

we're.definition: A shortened form of we are.

they're.definition: A shortened form of they are.

that's.definition: A shortened form of that is or that has.

there's.definition: A shortened form of there is or there has.

what's.definition: A shortened form of what is or what has.

who's.definition: A shortened form of who is or who has.

let's.definition: A shortened form of let us.

don't.definition: A shortened form of do not.

doesn't.definition: A shortened form of does not.

didn't.definition: A shortened form of did not.

isn't.definition: A shortened form of is not.

aren't.definition: A shortened form of are not.

wasn't.definition: A shortened form of was not.

weren't.definition: A shortened form of were not.

haven't.definition: A shortened form of have not.

hasn't.definition: A shortened form of has not.

hadn't.definition: A shortened form of had not.

couldn't.definition: A shortened form of could not.

won't.definition: A shortened form of will not.

wouldn't.definition: A shortened form of would not.

shouldn't.definition: A shortened form of should not.

mustn't.definition: A shortened form of must not.

mightn't.definition: A shortened form of might not.

needn't.definition: A shortened form of need not.

i've.definition: A shortened form of I have.

you've.definition: A shortened form of you have.

we've.definition: A shortened form of we have.

they've.definition: A shortened form of they have.

i'll.definition: A shortened form of I will.

you'll.definition: A shortened form of you will.

he'll.definition: A shortened form of he will.

she'll.definition: A shortened form of she will.

it'll.definition: A shortened form of it will.

we'll.definition: A shortened form of we will.

they'll.definition: A shortened form of they will.

i'd.definition: A shortened form of I would or I had.

you'd.definition: A shortened form of you would or you had.

he'd.definition: A shortened form of he would or he had.

she'd.definition: A shortened form of she would or she had.

we'd.definition: A shortened form of we would or we had.

they'd.definition: A shortened form of they would or they had.

have.definition: To possess or experience something; also an auxiliary verb used to form perfect tenses.
examples: She has a car. He has finished.

do.definition: To perform an action; also an auxiliary verb used in questions, negatives, and emphasis.

cannot.definition: The negative form of can: means to be unable to do something, or not permitted to do it.

no.definition: Expresses a negative answer, refusal, or the absence of something.
examples: No, thank you. There is no milk.
